svg.aria-label: GhostMesh testbed: weak points and attack surfaces. Same testbed. Red marks are where an attacker, a censor or a failure can hurt the mesh (threat-model.md §6–8)
svg.text: GhostMesh testbed: weak points and attack surfaces
Same testbed. Red marks are where an attacker, a censor or a failure can hurt the mesh (threat-model.md §6–8)
Integrity: who can change or forge
net · ps_N · sk_N · pks · W pk
end-to-end: pair key ck[e] (epoch DH ratchet) + XChaCha20-Poly1305
ESP-NOW broadcast · one Wi-Fi channel · every frame 240 B
every node also floods HELLO (2 s) and KEYS (~10 s); IDs rotate every 60 s
Pair keys from an epoch DH ratchet (FS + healing)
No destination in header; hop padding; ACK delay
Pseudonym + MAC rotate together every 60 s
Watchtower maps IDs but holds no X25519 keys
Integrity: who can change or forge
link_tag over every byte, checked first
AEAD tag, header fields bound as AD
Replay: caches, ±1 epoch, 5 s freshness, seq set
Flooding with k-suppression; backup path via D
Retries at 1/2/4 s, new msg_id each attempt
IPS detects in ≤ 5 s; BLOCK by node or pseudo+MAC
accepted and documented, or out of scope
Insider frames reach every parser; KEYS relayed before anyone checks them (O24)
Watchtower: locatable single point of failure; blocks lapse ~2 min without it (16c)
Boards that reboot while the watchtower is down stay mute until it returns (16b)
Watchtower → IPS log caps at ~120 frames/s; demo floods kept below it (16e)
CTRL verify budget can drop a TIME or BLOCK relayed via one neighbour (16d)
Low-and-slow evasion, baseline drift (16f); full spoof can mislead the operator (O9)
Provisioning laptop is the root of trust and holds every key (O16, out of scope)
Keys sit unencrypted in every board's flash; a seized board gives up its keys (O15)
One shared network_key: any captured board is an insider everywhere (O14)
4-board setup: relay D also holds the watchtower's secrets (O21)
Serial ports are unauthenticated; physical access means compromise (O16)
One fixed channel: jamming and junk floods are detected, not stopped (O17)
Timing and RSSI can reveal originators and track static boards (O1–O3)
Every board rotates at the same public moment; attacks can be timed to it (§8)
KEYS/CTRL can be jammed selectively (O18, O19); KEYS show the key graph (O23)
Stolen static key + forged KEYS frames takes over that board's pairs (A4, 10d)
